title: ENCOINS x Anastasia Labs: Zero-Knowledge Proof Trustless P2P Fiat-to-Crypto On-Ramp for Cardano

ms.promise:
Context: Trustless P2P on-ramp is a smart contract app that connects cryptocurrency sellers and buyers. A seller deposits funds into the smart contract and asks for a fiat payment. Once the payment is delivered, the buyer can generate a cryptographic proof and unlock the funds from the smart contract.
Task: Implement generic HTTPS API response pattern matching in zkFold Symbolic. It checks that the response from an API endpoint matches some JSON pattern and has the correct signature on it.
Outputs:
・Modules for arithmetic circuit generation for a JSON pattern match (Haskell)
・Modules for checking signatures on HTTPS responses and circuit generation from those checks (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
Acceptance:
・Modules for arithmetic circuit generation for a JSON pattern match can be found in the repo
・Modules for checking signatures on HTTPS responses and circuit generation from those checks can be found in the repo
・The progress report (pdf) will be shared with the reviewers
ms.report:
As the first milestone, we tasked ourselves with the following:
・Modules for arithmetic circuit generation for a JSON pattern match can be found in the repo
・Modules for checking signatures on HTTPS responses and circuit generation from those checks can be found in the repo

For context, in the Dapp, we allow users to withdraw funds provided that they submit the data from a JSON file of a particular structure together with the signature from our fintech partner. 
The particular data structure of interest (task 1) is implemented in https://github.com/zkFold/p2p-onramp/blob/main/src/ZkFold/P2P/Contract.hs. This module also contains an implementation of the signature verification protocol (task 2). Finally, the module contains an early prototype of our P2P on-ramp smart contract.
These artifacts heavily rely on our arithmetic circuit compiler that is split across many modules. We refer the reader to the folder https://github.com/zkFold/zkfold-base/blob/main/src/ZkFold/Symbolic/Compiler/. The compiler performs arithmetic circuit generation from a high-level code of a smart contract.
Together these modules give a complete solution to the Milestone 1 as it is possible to generate the circuit performing task 1 and task 2 using this code.
For more information we refer the reader to the following pieces of documentation. User documentation for smart contract developers: https://docs.zkfold.io/introduction/what-is-zkfold-symbolic. Developer documentation for contributors to zkFold Symbolic: https://hackage.haskell.org/package/zkfold-base-0.1.0.0/candidate.
The pdf version of this report can be found here:
https://github.com/zkFold/project-catalyst-reports/tree/main/P2P%20On-Ramp

Context: Trustless P2P on-ramp is a smart contract app that connects cryptocurrency sellers and buyers. A seller deposits funds into the smart contract and asks for a fiat payment. Once the payment is delivered, the buyer can generate a cryptographic proof and unlock the funds from the smart contract.
Task: Implement the on-chain code (zkFold Symbolic smart contract).
Outputs:
・Modules for Trustless P2P On-ramp smart contract on-chain code (Haskell)
ms.criteria:
Acceptance:
・Modules for Trustless P2P On-ramp smart contract can be found in the repo
・The progress report (pdf) will be shared with the reviewers
ms.report:
We resubmit the POA with minor code corrections. We have implemented the on-chain code (zkFold Symbolic smart contract):

1. Modules for Trustless P2P On-ramp smart contract can be found in the repo:

https://github.com/zkFold/p2p-onramp/blob/vlasin-catalyst-m3-version2/src/ZkFold/Cardano/UPLC/OnRamp.hs

2. The progress report (pdf) has been shared with the reviewers:

https://github.com/zkFold/project-catalyst-reports/blob/main/P2P%20On-Ramp/1100125%20-%20M3%20-%20progress%20report.pdf

------------------------------------------------

One of the reviewers provided us with a list of suggested modifications. After careful consideration between zkFold and Anastasia Labs teams, we came to the conclusion that not all of these modifications are necessary for the security of the contract. Here are our responses:

1. Output Position Verification: Ensure outputs are identified by address rather than position, as the order of txInfoOutputs may not be guaranteed.

It is the intended behavior that the order of outputs is chosen by the user.

2. Clearer Trace Messages: Replace messages like "rollup: no input" with more descriptive error messages to aid debugging (e.g., "Error: Missing OnRamp Input").

Error messages were updated.

3. Signature Verification Compatibility: Double-check that dataToBlake produces the correct hash format expected by verifyEd25519Signature to avoid verification failures.

`verifyEd25519Signature` function can verify a signature on any message. One may verify that the code compiles successfully.

4. Timelock Validation in Update: Ensure timelock is set in Update to confirm locking period consistency.

The lines related to the timelock were updated. The details can be found in the comments to the code.

5. Define untypedOnRamp Behavior Explicitly: Validate that it meets Plutus expectations to avoid accidental misinterpretation.

The function `untypedOnRamp` is well-defined. The code compiles successfully, including the PlutusTx plugin.
